# rollcall-guard-act-committee-vote-2026-04-30
- **URL:** https://rollcall.com/2026/04/30/ban-on-kids-companion-chatbots-advanced-by-senate-committee/ · **Accessed:** 2026-09-16 · **For:** v2→v3 response round, slice L
- **What it establishes:** Roll Call, April 30, 2026. Source for the 22–0 Senate Judiciary vote AND for the fact that an amendment adopted at markup narrowed the age-verification requirements to companion chatbots. Also notes the amendment softened the criminal prohibition and removed the 30-minute re-disclosure requirement. Corroborated by Senator Hawley's press release of the same day (https://www.hawley.senate.gov/senator-hawleys-guard-act-to-protect-kids-from-ai-chatbots-passes-committee-unanimously/ : "the Senate Judiciary Committee unanimously passed Senator Hawley’s GUARD Act"; it "bans AI companions for minors and mandates AI chatbots to disclose their non-human and non-professional status").
- **Key passages:**
  - "The Judiciary Committee voted 22-0 to approve the bill, which would make it a crime to knowingly provide a chatbot that engages minors in sexually explicit behavior or coerces them to die by suicide."
  - "An amendment was adopted during the markup and released afterwards that made the bill’s age-verification requirements apply only to companion chatbots, rather than more general models, and softened the criminal prohibition on chatbots engaging in sexual conversations with minors."
  - "The bill, after the amendment, would require companion chatbot providers to verify ages using government-issued identification, other forms of identification corroborated by documentation, or similar information provided to a financial institution, a device operating system or app store."
- **Reliability:** Congressional trade press; independent; consistent with the GPO text.
- **Relevance to this project:** L5: the 22–0 vote (April 30, 2026) is CONFIRMED; the narrowing amendment is the nuance the review's summary missed.
